attempts.summary: On node1, created datauser and a dedicated loop-backed XFS filesystem mounted at /srv/data (backed by /var/lib/srv-data/srv-data.img, persisted via /etc/fstab with `loop,uquota,usrquota` options). Set an XFS user quota for datauser (bsoft=95m, bhard=100m) so the filesystem itself enforces the 100MB limit. Verified enforcement by writing 150MB as datauser and observing the write stopped at exactly 100MB with a "Disk quota exceeded" error, then cleaned up the test file. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy quota/mount state, issued `shutdown -r now`, polled until SSH returned, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual reboot, not just a service restart), and re-verified post-restart that the mount, quota configuration, and enforcement (write capped at 100MB) all recovered correctly.
